messages.content: What is RobustFloat?

RobustFloat is a floating-waste detection system for inland-water imagery. It uses YOLO26s-P2 Unified as the computer-vision detector and combines structured detection data with retrieval-augmented generation for grounded responses.
Which model is the current primary model?
The current primary model is YOLO26s-P2 Unified, trained jointly on TUD-GV and IWHR with one class, floating_waste.
What was the final YOLO26s-P2 Unified performance on TUD-GV?
On the TUD-GV test set, YOLO26s-P2 Unified achieved Precision 97.32%, Recall 90.37%, F1 93.72%, mAP@50 93.60%, and mAP@50–95 71.99% at a confidence threshold of 0.25.
What was the final YOLO26s-P2 Unified performance on IWHR?
On the IWHR test set, YOLO26s-P2 Unified achieved Precision 86.61%, Recall 68.76%, F1 76.66%, mAP@50 73.48%, and mAP@50–95 51.78% at a confidence threshold of 0.25.
Can the number of detections be treated as the exact amount of waste in the water?

No. The detection count represents objects detected by the model at the selected confidence threshold. It should not be interpreted as the exact physical amount of waste because the detector can miss objects.
What is domain shift in this project?

Domain shift means that the visual distribution of a new dataset differs from the data used to train the model. In RobustFloat, the strong difference between TUD-GV and IWHR performance demonstrates that floating-waste detection is affected by domain differences.
What happens when the TUD-only model is tested on IWHR?
The compute-matched YOLO26s-P2 TUD-only model achieved Precision 31.40%, Recall 15.68%, F1 20.92%, mAP@50 7.39%, and mAP@50–95 3.70% on IWHR. This indicates substantial cross-domain degradation.
Does YOLO26s-P2 Unified outperform the IWHR-only model on IWHR?

No. In the controlled comparison, the unified model achieved 76.66% F1 on IWHR, while the IWHR-only model achieved 77.36% F1. The unified model's advantage is that one model serves both domains rather than requiring separate domain-specific models.
Does a confidence score of 0.90 mean the model is 90% certain that the detection is correct?

No. Detector confidence should not be interpreted directly as a calibrated probability of correctness. RobustFloat should use empirically calibrated confidence bins when presenting reliability information.
What should the chatbot say when it does not have enough information to answer a question?

The chatbot should say that it does not have sufficient project data to answer the question rather than inventing an answer. It should only use facts supplied by the structured database and retrieved project knowledge.
